$comment: `bridge`: the last PUBLISHED release that still runs every conversion below; upgrade.json `minFrom` (the support floor) may point at it. Registry of every one-time conversion the core still carries (docs/MIGRATIONS.md). `removableAtFloor`: once upgrade.json `minFrom` reaches this version, every site has already run the conversion in a bridge release, so the code MUST be gone (tests/core/migration-registry.test.mjs fails otherwise). null = not removable by a floor raise (reason given). `present`: files or code symbols that prove the code still exists. `removed`: conversions already deleted, with the floor that made it safe.

active.what: Start-up sweep: pending module data conversions (dataVersion contract), empty legacy settings, old choice texts; runs once per state (core.legacySweepState).
active.why: Permanent contract: a module declares dataVersion and its migrations; the sweep resumes interrupted ones.

active.what: Old menu (instances shown in the menu + nav.custom) frozen into nav.menu when an instance is created or the navigation page opens; legacy fallback while nav.menu is absent (restored old backup, brand-new site).
active.why: Kept at the 0.6.18 floor raise on purpose. The start-up call is long gone and every site that updates went through it, but the fallback is also the reader of BACKUP FILES made before the stored menu (nav.menu, 0.2.6): a backup file never expires (docs/MIGRATIONS.md rule 5, no minimum version on restore), and restoring one relies on loadMenu / menuResolve rebuilding the menu from showInNav + nav.custom. Removable only after a backup-format decision (refuse such backups with a clear message, or freeze the menu inside the restore), like legacy-off.

active.what: Restoring a backup made before 0.1.20: modules/instances that were switched off become uninstalled, data kept.

removed.what: One-time freeze of overlay placements of existing instances (0.2.6).
Start-up call that froze the menu into nav.menu (the freeze itself stays, see menu-freeze).
